articles.title: Gears of War: E-Day-Themed Xbox Controller Is Up for Preorder
articles.summary: Microsoft is releasing a new limited-edition controller decked out with Gears of War: E-Day imagery to coincide with the game's release.
articles.body:
Update Sept 29 : The controller is out tomorrow, September 30, and both Amazon and Walmart are offering a $6 discount, bringing the price down to $84. Still not cheap, but you might as well save $6 if you're going to buy it anyway. Also, the matching 8BitDo charger has sold out at Amazon but is still available from 8BitDo .

Gears of War: E-Day is Microsoft’s major Xbox exclusive for the fall. Set 14 years before the first Gears of War, it’s a prequel to the gritty chainsaw-slinging series that helped make the Xbox 360 the best console of its generation. To go along with E-Day in the Xbox Series X|S era, Microsoft is releasing a limited-edition Gears of War: E-Day-themed wireless controller. It costs $89.99 is set to release on September 30. Preorders are live now at Amazon and all the other major retailers.

Gears of War: E-Day Limited Edition Xbox Wireless Controller

E-Day in the Gears universe stands for “Emergence Day.” That’s the day when the Locust Horde emerged from underground on the planet Sera and attacked humanity, setting off the titular conflict in Gears of War. That’s what the upcoming game will cover , and that’s what this controller’s design reflects.

The controller is black, with a gaping red hole opening on its faceplate, the cracks of which spread down the grips. It’s a bold design, complete with “3D molded, laser-etched details,” meaning you can actually feel the cracks. The series’ iconic skull image, the Crimson Omen, is emblazoned in the center of the red hole. Both triggers are made of transparent red plastic, and all of the face buttons (save for the Xbox button) are unlabeled, which is pretty cool.

8BitDo Ultimate Charging Dock for Xbox Controllers, Gears of War: E-Day

In addition to the controller, 8BitDo is releasing an officially licensed Gears of War: E-Day-themed controller dock. It has the name of the game on it, plus red cracks that line up nicely with the design of the controller, so it looks great on your shelf or coffee table while you charge it. The dock comes with a rechargeable battery pack, so you don’t need to anything else to charge up the controller. Unfortunately, it's currently sold out at Amazon.

The Art and Making of Gears of War: E-Day

For more, check out our comprehensive Gears of War: E-Day preorder guide , which goes into detail about what comes in each edition of the game.

Chris Reed is a commerce editor and deals expert for IGN. He also runs IGN's board game and LEGO coverage. You can follow him on Bluesky .

articles.title: Where to Buy Pokémon Cards in 2026
articles.summary: Trying to buy Pokémon cards in 2026 without significant markup? Here is where to find Booster Bundles, ETBs, and restocks at MSRP or "market price" from Amazon, Target, and Walmart.
articles.body:
Finding Pokémon cards in 2026 is just as hard as it's ever been, especially at MSRP. Between Ascended Heroes being what feels like the most popular we've seen since Destined Rivals , and the 30th Anniversary release in September, Pokémon isn't exactly an easy hobby to have these days; especially for the more casual fans out there chasing some high-value cards .

If you're trying to keep up with Pokémon TCG without getting ripped off or left behind, here's where to start, including the latest update on what can be bought right now from trusted US retailers.

Pokémon TCG - Sold and Shipped by Amazon Finder

Pokémon TCG: Mega Evolution—Pitch Black Elite Trainer Box

Pokémon TCG: Mega Evolution—Ascended Heroes Booster Bundle

Pokémon TCG: Mega Evolution—Pitch Black Booster Bundle

Pokémon TCG: Mega Evolution—Chaos Rising Booster Bundle

Pokémon TCG: Mega Evolution—Perfect Order Booster Bundle

2024 Pokémon TCG World Championships Deck (One Random Deck)

Let's quickly check out the latest Pokémon TCG deals that are floating around online right now. The best and most popular pick right now is Pitch Black Booster Bundles for just $50, alongside Pitch Black ETBs for just $70 , both available with no fuss from Amazon.

To see all the recently restocked items at Amazon, be sure to check out our custom search tracker to ensure you're buying sealed boosters that are only "sold and shipped" directly from Amazon itself.

When it comes to buying Pokémon cards, it's best to know what sites you can trust, especially among the major retailers. For those just starting out, here's a quick cheat sheet on what retailers you should frequent often when looking for the best times to buy.

For the most casual fans out there I recommend sticking to TCGplayer, Amazon, and then your local stores for any of your TCG purchases. TCGplayer is the most trustworthy resale marketplace online, and while you're still paying above and beyond (i.e. above MSRP, almost always), it's still worth considering.

Amazon also typically always has at least some Pokémon TCG sets in stock these days, even if, just like TCGplayer, they are above MSRP. We'll discuss "Market Price" a little more in a bit, but for now, it's simply the way things are with Pokémon TCG. For those looking for an easy experience, "market" rate is what you have to pay, you either get with it, or miss out entirely. Well, not entirely, but it becomes a whole lot more of a headache to navigate, that's for sure.

As I mentioned earlier, we have a dedicated custom search tracker to ensure you're buying sealed boosters that are only "sold and shipped" directly from Amazon itself. That avoids any untrustworthy third party sellers, and ensures you're getting fast Prime delivery as well.

Pokémon TCG: 2026 Release Calendar – At a Glance

It's easy to list them off, a lot harder to find in practice. But, I'll do what I can to help. In the US, The Pokémon Center, Walmart, Target, and Best Buy all typically have Pokémon TCG drops at some time or another.

Walmart likes to lock these behind its paid Walmart+ membership, while Best Buy tends to drop these as "app exclusives" with a login required to access. Target just drops them whenever it feels like it, so you have to be primed and ready to buy.

As this is just my day job, I don't typically have the time (like most people) to be hanging around waiting for a drop to then write up an article before they inevitably sell out before I can hit publish.

While I update the "Live" tracker we have above, this is typically focused on Amazon for the rest of the casual fans like myself. Instead, if you're serious about only paying MSRP and nothing else, I suggest following any of the following on X/Twitter:

All of these accounts are fairly on it, and tend to post stuff as soon as it becomes available. Stick notifications on, and you're well away.

It's unfortunately hard to find Pokémon TCG at MSRP. Market value is often the price you have to pay now, even from big retailers like Amazon, as I mentioned.

But is it worth it? Only you can be the judge of that.

The "market price" is often dictated by what the majority of people are willing to pay, but only you can decide if this if truly worth your money. You can easily find a good idea of what the current rate is for any particular set or card by looking at the data on TCGplayer.

So what's the difference between this and scalping? I guess... perspective? It's a hard distinction to make, in all honesty, but I'll still never judge anyone for buying overpriced sealed products from TCGplayer or Amazon. What's important is that you get to make the choice on where you buy from, and how much effort you want to put in when collecting Pokémon cards.

articles.title: 15 Studio Ghibli Movies Are Getting Blu-ray Steelbook Reprints, and They're Out Today
articles.body:
The Studio Ghibli animated films have been released a number of times on physical media. The most recent Blu-ray release came in brightly colored limited-edition steelbooks, but they've gone out of stock – which is undoubtedly why they’re getting reprinted. The whole batch of 15 Ghibli films is back, and they're out today, September 29.

We’re talking movies like Spirited Away, My Neighbor Totoro, Princess Mononoke, and most of the rest of the studio’s output over the past 40 years. Many of these are straight-up masterpieces of animation. So if you’ve been eager to add some of these to your collection, now is a good time to do so.

Preorder the Studio Ghibli Limited-Edition Reprints

My Neighbor Totoro: Limited Edition Steelbook

Spirited Away: Limited Edition Steelbook

Princess Mononoke: Limited Edition Steelbook

Kiki's Delivery Service: Limited Edition Steelbook

Howl's Moving Castle: Limited Edition Steelbook

Grave Of The Fireflies: Limited Edition Steelbook

Nausicaä Of The Valley Of The Wind: Limited Edition

From Up On Poppy Hill: Limited Edition Steelbook

When Marnie Was There: Limited Edition Steelbook

The Wind Rises: Limited Edition Steelbook

The Secret World Of Arrietty: Limited Edition Steelbook

Only Yesterday: Limited Edition Steelbook

The Tale Of The Princess Kaguya: Limited Edition Steelbook

Most of these movies were written and directed by either Hayao Miyazaki or Isao Takahata. They’re all gorgeous to look at and sport high-caliber English voice work, with names like Cate Blanchett, Christian Bale, Edward James Olmos, Emily Blunt, Cary Elwes, Gillian Anderson, Jamie Lee Curtis, Amy Poehler, Dev Patel, Daisy Ridley, Hailee Steinfeld, Kiernan Shipka, and more showing up in the credits.

I’ve only seen a handful of these movies, but they were all at least good , and most of them were spectacular. My Neighbor Totoro is about a pair of kids with a neglectful — er, busy — dad who move to a new house and discover strange creatures that live in or near the house. Spirited Away is a gentle nightmare of a film, about a girl whose parents transform into pigs and she gets lost in a town filled with strange people and beasts.

So if you could use some high quality animation in your life, these Blu-ray steelbook editions would make a great addition to your collection.

articles.title: The Witcher 3 Fans Relieved to Find Low-Polygon Pigeons Have Survived the Remaster Process
articles.summary: The Witcher 3 Remastered brings tons of graphics improvements, but developer CD Projekt Red has left one incredibly important creature as it was: the pigeon.
articles.body:
The Witcher 3 Remastered brings tons of graphics improvements, but developer CD Projekt Red has left one incredibly important creature as it was: the pigeon.

Ahead of the remaster's public release, updated pigeon models were found in the game, but it only seems to apply to pigeons that are hanging out on the ground. Still, some people were upset with the assumed change, with one person posting the new ground-based model with the old flying one in a Reddit post captioned, "Gone, but never forgotten."

Luckily, it seems like the beloved low-poly pigeon has survived the remaster, as it was spotted by Kotaku Editor-in-Chief Ethan Gach on X / Twitter out in the wild. Apparently, The Witcher 3 uses different pigeon models for flying and grounded birds! If anything, the low-polygon pigeon looks even funnier in the remaster, as it shows the (lack of) detail even better with the updated lighting.

This is a false alarm. Street pigeons have always been different from the ones flying. pic.twitter.com/6JFGuzZ7K2 — AmericanTruckSongs9 (@ethangach) September 28, 2026

This is a false alarm. Street pigeons have always been different from the ones flying. pic.twitter.com/6JFGuzZ7K2

So, even though The Witcher 3 Remastered came with a whole host of graphics improvements, it does seem like some old assets have kept their place in the game. Hopefully, CD Projekt Red also kept in some of the low-detail food in the game as well.

The Witcher 3 Remastered has only been out a few hours, but it's already breaking player records . It's broken the 11-year-old game's peak Steam concurrent player count, and the number looks set to rise further as we get closer to the weekend.

The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt - Remastered is available as a free update on PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and Nintendo Switch 2. To ease you into Geralt’s life on the road, check out the things The Witcher 3 doesn’t tell you , plus IGN’s The Witcher 3 walkthrough and The Witcher 3 endings guide, which outlines all of the major quests and choices in the base game and expansions (now bundled in with the Remastered edition). When you’re ready for the tough choices, check out our The Witcher 3 sex and romance guide to see who Geralt can smooch and all the opportunities to do so. And to make Geralt as strong a monster hunter as possible, check out all the Witcher gear locations , Places of Power locations , and even Gwent card locations .

articles.title: Why Control Resonant Developer Remedy Avoided Using Yellow Paint to Guide Players
articles.summary: Control Resonant's director has explained how the team chose to handle exploration in a way that doesn't feel like it is holding the player's hand with things like yellow paint.
articles.body:
Control Resonant's director has explained how the team chose to handle exploration in a way that doesn't feel like it is holding the player's hand with things like yellow paint.

For a number of years now, some gamers have begun to feel like games provide players with more guidance than is necessary. One example of this is yellow paint, which basically highlights exactly where the player needs to go during exploration. Critics say that when this sort of navigation aid is heavy handed, it can be distracting and remove a sense of agency. Marvel's Wolverine, for example, was heavily criticized for its "fart gas," a blue mist that Wolverine can sniff out to find his objective. Soon after launch, developer Insomniac added the ability to toggle it off .

Control Resonant developer Remedy doesn't beat players over the head. It is an open-world game with zones that the player can freely explore, though sometimes it isn't always crystal clear where to go. Control Resonant director Mikael Kasurinen explained on the Dropped Frames podcast (via Kotaku ) that it was important for the player to feel like they were figuring out this convoluted world themselves, rather than following flashing arrows. He noted that for players to get the most out of the world, they had to be active participants.

Control Resonant - June 2026 Screenshots

“It’s so important that the players feel like they’re the ones figuring it out,” said Kasurinen. “It’s the job of us as creators to… I mean, it is a crafted experience at the end of the day, right? You have to find the right balance between ‘here’s the world’ and ‘here are the different themes and elements that you have to pay attention to.’ But it has to feel like it’s on you to make a decision on what to do with those elements that you see within the world. If it feels like it’s like ‘go here,’ it’s not anymore a decision for the player. Somebody already decided for you.”

The director went on to note that Remedy recognized that it risked alienating players looking for a more guided and simple experience, but for those that really engage with it, it will be more rewarding and interesting.

“People will be coming back to this game, exploring, trying to kind of find out things and so on," he added. "It’s not something that you kind of go through, you did what you were told, and you’re done. It feels like, no, I made some choices in this game and you have that little little question: Did I make the right choices? And I want that f***ing question. I want people to think like that. I want them to kind of, you know, doubt, go back, check again, see what they could do differently, because that’s life. That’s what makes it sticky and interesting.”

Another developer with a similar philosophy to Remedy's is Warlock: Dungeons & Dragons studio Invoke. Dominic Guay, General Manager at Invoke Studios, told IGN at gamescom 2026 that the developers avoided putting waypoints into the game because they want players to actually explore .

The open-world single-player action-adventure goes easy on the hand-holding by ditching traditional quest markers that guide players directly from one story section to the next. While it does have a compass on the top of the screen — which you can turn off — the player is left to work out where to go by exploring, talking to NPCs, and thinking about what to do next.

“We wanted them to engage with the world, to figure things out and feel that when they found things, it was based on their actions and not just blindly trusting a waypoint,” Guay said.

IGN's Control Resonant review returned an 8/10. We said: "Even when combat's sharp edge eventually dulls, Control Resonant is a great addition to the Remedyverse," reads an excerpt from the review. "While its story follows a more standard framework, its gravitational pull is in the inventive world built around it and the humanization that grounds the paranatural intrigue."

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: The Steam Frame: VR’s Future or the Beginning of the End?
articles.body:
I’ve always loved VR. I bought my current headset – a Pico 4 – three years ago, for around £300/$400. While that particular model isn’t available in America for very questionable reasons , if I wanted an alternative and was willing to enter Zuckerberg’s walled garden (I am not), a Quest 3S is even cheaper. With good wireless support, color pass-through cameras and a robust native library of games even before connecting to a PC, I felt VR had finally arrived at where it should be. A new world of games, accessible for less than a Nintendo Switch 2.

While I understand RAM prices are skyrocketing, when Valve announced its entry into the lightweight, wireless VR field would cost a wallet-obliterating £889/$1,059 for the cheapest Steam Frame model , my heart sank. And worse yet, it wasn’t launching any new software to accompany it. The Steam Frame’s killer app? A native port of Half-Life: Alyx, an admittedly excellent game, but one released in 2020 with a mod scene that has largely moved on due to lack of support from Valve itself.

Even the store page for the Steam Frame proudly displays Moss Book 2 as one of the great games you could play on the Frame. And while it is great (as are many VR games – there’s a library here dwarfing any console for sure), the developers, Polyarc, recently closed its doors due to a lack of sales and funding, even after releasing a non-VR version. While there’s still a steady trickle of VR games, on the PC side of things, almost all the big players have tapped out. There are no big AAA releases to look forward to. No big next step for VR design. And the buy-in price to access this via Valve’s new hardware is triple what I’d be willing to pay for a headset. Quadruple that, in the case of Meta’s newly-announced lightweight VR glasses .

Despite all this, I love VR. It has filled the hole in my life where lightgun games and oddball titles with one-off peripherals (pour one out for Samba De Amigo and Steel Battalion) used to live. It features some of the coolest mech games , most terrifying trips through haunted wastelands and experimental arcade experiences around. VR isn’t going anywhere, with a slow but steady flow of new hardware and modders continually patching VR support into older classic games . But I also cannot fathom what the future of VR looks like, or if it even has one at all.

If Valve and Meta are to be believed, VR isn’t an alternative to a lower-end handheld console. It is the domain of enthusiast tech nerds with money to burn. It is a whole medium with almost no major studios involved anymore, and even Meta’s big announcement showcase last week featured little more than rehashes and ports of ‘classic’ games, and many of those will remain exclusive to Meta hardware too. Valve has all the money in the world but without investing some of it into developers, I worry that unless the Frame sells unexpectedly well, that it too will lose interest in this field.

While I love my cheap, versatile little headset, and adore adding VR mods to classic games to experience them in new ways , I’d like for VR to grow and be supported once more. To be able to point to something big and new and exciting on the horizon to get other people on board with me. And a port of a six-year-old game, however good it was, isn’t going to cut it.

Steam Hype is the latest site in the Hookshot network, joining Nintendo Life , Push Square , Pure Xbox and the retro-centric Time Extension to cover all corners of the gaming universe. Hookshot is also partnered with the tech experts at Digital Foundry and is partnered commercially with IGN. As Hookshot’s dedicated PC gaming site, it’s got news of the latest releases , updates and mod drops , plus weekly roundups and a must-play monthly playlist to help you keep up with the never-ending deluge of new experiences.

articles.title: 50-Minute AI-Generated Doctor Who Episode Is 'Pretty Good,' BBC Boss Says
articles.summary: The BBC's new director general has described an AI-generated Doctor Who episode as "pretty good," and suggested that the technology enabled the creation of content "at the standard of a Hollywood studio."
articles.body:
The BBC's new director general has described a 50-minute AI-generated episode of Doctor Who as "pretty good," and suggested that the technology now enabled the creation of content "at the standard of a Hollywood studio."

Brittin became boss of the UK's iconic broadcasting company in May this year, after almost two decades at Google, where he wound up working as the company's UK managing director.

Now in charge of the BBC, Brittin faces a tough task of making further drastic cuts to the corporation's spending, while it continues to try and produce world-class programming — including its flagship sci-fi adventure series that's currently on hiatus after a disastrous few years.

The 25 Most Essential Doctor Who Episodes

Doctor Who fans largely agree that their favorite show has declined in quality over the years, but especially over the past two seasons which featured Ncuti Gatwa in the role, and the return of Russell T Davies as showrunner. After just two seasons, this era of the show was unceremoniously ended when co-funding partner Disney ditched the series, prompting the departure of Gatwa in a reshot ending. A later promise to mount a one-off Christmas special that could tie-up the era's remaining plotlines was later scrapped too, with Davies and production company Bad Wolf also exiting.

Now, the BBC has begun looking for a fresh production house to take the show on — a process it wants to result in new episodes of the series arriving in either 2028 or 2029.

"Somebody sent me a 50-minute episode of Doctor Who that was AI-generated the other day," Brittin said, speaking at the Royal Television Society conference in London this week (thanks, Variety ). "It's pretty good. I mean, it's not going to replace humans, and we'll come on to that

"So everyone's a creator. Not all the creativity is bad," Brittin continued. "Everyone's got the ability in their hands — or six billion people have — to create content at the standard of a Hollywood studio."

While Brittin does not name the AI project he watched, it is almost certainly the 50-minute first episode of fan-made project The Unmade Season , which features a AI-made continuation of the series. Having watched a chunk of this myself, I'd say it is as good as you'd expect AI to be — which is to say, almost photorealistic but narratively still pretty flawed. The show picks up with a new incarnation of the Doctor who regenerates from David Tennant's 14th Doctor, played a Scottish-sounding AI actor. Scenes feature various AI oddities, though also incorporate various familiar Doctor Who monsters, such as Slitheen and Ood.

All in all, it's not very good. And as a Doctor Who fan, it is particularly odd to hear the boss of the BBC offering any sort of praise to content, even non-commercial fan content, that appears to have been generated by regurgitating the BBC's own copyrighted episodes.

While budgets may be tight, here's hoping this is the extent of the BBC's relationship to AI with Doctor Who going forward.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

articles.title: Game of Thrones Movie Aegon’s Conquest Sets 2029 Release Date With Director Owen Harris
articles.summary: Warner Bros. has officially set a June 1, 2029 release date for Game of Thrones: Aegon's Conquest, with Owen Harris attached to direct.
articles.body:
Warner Bros. has officially announced a release date and director for Game of Thrones: Aegon’s Conquest , the first feature film to stem from the HBO franchise.

Game of Thrones: Aegon’s Conquest will open in theaters on June 9, 2029. Owen Harris will direct from a screenplay by Beau Willimon (House of Cards). The film will adapt material from George R.R. Martin’s Targaryen history book, Fire & Blood.

Harris is no stranger to Game of Thrones, having directed episodes of A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms . Harris also directed three acclaimed episodes of Black Mirror ("Be Right Back", "San Junipero", and "Striking Vipers").

Martin’s Fire & Blood chronicles the history of the dragon-riding Targaryen dynasty, including the Dance of the Dragons civil war depicted in House of the Dragon . The Targaryens arrived in Westeros following the Doom of Valyria , settling on the island of Dragonstone . By the time Aegon reached adulthood, he made it his mission to unite the long-warring Seven Kingdoms under the rule of one man: himself.

Aegon I Targaryen is responsible for countless deaths in his quest to become the sole ruler of the realm. He’s aided by his sister-wives Visenya and Rhaenys. All three siblings fly fearsome dragons: Aegon rides Balerion the Black Dread , Visenya rides Vhagar (yes, the same giant beast flown by Aemond in House of the Dragon ), and Rhaenys flies Meraxes.

Aegon battles a slew of kingdoms during the Conquest, but his two biggest adversaries are King Harren the Black, the wicked lord of Harrenhal , and Meria Martell, the princess of Dorne. Meria and Dorne’s resistance against Aegon the Conqueror was notably recalled by Ormund Hightower to Daeron Targaryen in House of the Dragon Season 3, Episode 5.

The Game of Thrones series has established that Aegon knew about the White Walkers and passed this secret knowledge down the generations from ruler to ruler. Aegon foresaw a great looming terror in the North, which convinced him that a Targaryen must occupy the Iron Throne when that dark day arrives to ensure humanity’s survival.

Bringing Aegon’s Conquest to the big screen poses a host of challenges for the filmmakers, several of which I break down here .

articles.title: Everything Coming to Apple TV in October
articles.body:
Unlike streaming services like Peacock and Disney+ , Apple TV isn’t really leaning into the Halloween vibes this year. Instead, the streaming platform is opting to stay the usual course of prestige original shows, movies, and documentaries. It is, however, still home to the Peanuts holiday specials, and even if you aren’t a subscriber, you’ll be able to watch "It's the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown" for free the weekend of Saturday, October 17.

If you are subscribed to Apple TV, however, here’s what else you have to look forward to next month.

New Series and Movies Coming to Apple TV in October

Apple TV is getting one new documentary in October, which happens to be one of two new additions about climbing. Directed by Amir Bar-Lev, The Last First: Winter K2 was filmed back in 2021, when a group of climbers tried to ascend the titular second-highest mountain on Earth. The documentary will be coming to Apple TV after its premiere at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival.

The Sisters Grimm Season 2 - Premieres October 2

One of the only family-friendly additions of the month, The Sisters Grimm is premiering its second season on October 2. The animated series, which is based on Michael Buckley’s graphic novels, follows two relatively modern sisters who discover a town full of fairy tales.

Apple TV might be known for its thrillers and sci-fi, but it’s also home to some genre-bending comedies like Widow’s Bay. Hoping to join the better ranks of that list is Small Prophets, a six-part series that follows an aging man who turns to alchemy and magical spirits to find his one true love. Despite premiering on BBC Two earlier this year, unfortunately this one won’t be available to UK subscribers until 2027.

A series of projects based on various Mattel toys got the green light after the success of Greta Gerwig’s Barbie . One of those projects is now coming to fruition as Matchbox the Movie, inspired by the titular toy car line. John Cena stars as Sean, an undercover CIA agent who enlists his childhood friend group to help save the world.

Where’s Wanda? Season 2 - Premieres October 21

The darkly funny German series Where’s Wanda is returning for a second season toward the end of the month. While Carlotta and Deda managed to get some semblance of their lives back in Season 1, yet another crisis with their daughter, Wanda, threatens to tear their family apart again.

Tenzing is based on the true story of Tenzing Norgay and Sir Edmund Hillary, the first climbers to summit Mount Everest. Genden Phuntsok and Tom Hiddleston as the legendary climbers, who have their worldviews challenged by both the harrowing climb and each other. The film will receive a limited theatrical release starting October 9 before its Apple TV streaming premiere on October 16.

An entirely new Apple Original series, Nocturne is loosely based on the Joona Linna crime novels by Lars Kepler, the pen name for Alexander Ahndoril and Alexandra Coelho Ahndoril. It stars Liev Schreiber as Jonah Lynn, a detective who heads to a small Pennsylvania town embroiled in the threat of a serial killer’s return.

Dark Matter: Season 2, Episode 6 - “What the Universe is Made of”

Slow Horses: Season 6, Episode 4 - “Lost and Found”

Dark Matter: Season 2, Episode 7 - “The Pyramid”

Slow Horses: Season 6, Episode 5 - “Sayonara”

Dark Matter: Season 2, Episode 8 - “The Basic Oneness of Everything”

"It's the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown" (Streaming for Free)

Slow Horses: Season 6 - “Judgement Day” (Final)

Dark Matter: Season 2, Episode 9 - “How to Build the Box”

Dark Matter: Season 2, Episode 10 - “No Quiet Life”

Apple TV continues to offer one ad-free subscription plan at $14.99/month, though that plan is now included in iCloud+ memberships . The service also recently launched its first official bundle with Peacock , which knocks about 30% off the standard price of having both subscriptions.

If you’re just looking for a taster (or a specific binge-watch), Apple TV is one of the only remaining streaming services to offer a full seven-day free trial . Extended free trials are also included in most Apple purchases, including the new line of iPhones .

articles.title: The Pokémon Deluxe Character Guide Book Drops to a New Low Price on Amazon
articles.summary: Another fun way to celebrate Pokémon's 30th anniversary is getting a Pokédex for your shelf.
articles.body:
Amazon has dropped the price of the Pokémon Deluxe Character Guide to $39.84, a whopping 34% off what it retails for. This is the lowest price we've ever seen on this book, which was released only a month ago.

The latest discount on the book arrives a week before Amazon's Prime Big Deal Days sale , but unlike other early discounts, it doesn't appear to require an Amazon Prime subscription.

Pokémon Deluxe Character Guide (Hardcover)

While this is the lowest price we've ever seen on this book, Amazon has been discounting it since before it even came out. IGN covered the preorders for the Deluxe Character Guide and saw it drop down to $41.99 before it officially released on August 25. So while an extra $2 off isn't much, this book is cool enough that any discount is notable — especially with all of the ongoing Pokémon 30th anniversary celebrations in 2026.

We had the chance to go hands-on with the book earlier this month and loved everything about it. IGN's reviewer, Blythe Dujardin , went into detail about what to expect from the Pokémon character book and there's a lot to love about it. Every single Pokémon gets an entry, alongside stats and everything else you'd find in your Pokédex about them. Some of the more popular Pokémon get quite a bit more, including bits of their history in games, TCG, and the anime.

Should You Wait for Prime Big Deal Days?

With Amazon's October Prime Day sale kicking off on October 6 , you may be wondering if you should wait until then to buy this Pokémon Deluxe Character Guide. While it's certainly possible the price could drop further next week, it's fairly unlikely. One of the best times to buy books at a discount is the week before a Prime-exclusive sale because that seems to be when Amazon kicks off most of its book deals .

With that being said, it seems highly possible this book could get a bigger discount in November when Black Friday season rolls around. So if you want to try to save a few more bucks, it's probably worth waiting until then to pull the trigger on this one.

articles.title: Coinbase Joins Pokémon TCG Hype With Its Own Digital Pack-Opening Service
articles.summary: Coinbase is joining the Pokémon TCG craze with its own digital pack-opening platform.
articles.body:
Coinbase is joining the Pokémon TCG craze with its own digital pack-opening platform.

Coinbase, a US-based cryptocurrency exchange platform, is moving in on the TCG market with a particular focus on Pokémon. At least, that’s what it seems like, based on a tweet it published on September 28.

“Your binder is about to get a major upgrade,” the post reads. “Rip packs on your phone. Every pull backed by a real, physical card. Vault it or ship it. Soon on Coinbase.”

Your binder is about to get a major upgrade. Rip packs on your phone. Every pull backed by a real, physical card. Vault it or ship it. Soon on Coinbase. pic.twitter.com/Utfwq30DSj — Coinbase 🛡️ (@coinbase) September 28, 2026

Your binder is about to get a major upgrade. Rip packs on your phone. Every pull backed by a real, physical card. Vault it or ship it. Soon on Coinbase. pic.twitter.com/Utfwq30DSj

While the post’s text doesn’t mention Pokémon by name, the accompanying image attached to it shows mockups of five Pokémon TCG card packs that are labeled ‘Pokémon’ with the numbers 1-5.

The platform also responded to a few comments that mentioned the popular monster-catching franchise; one user wrote, “Pokémon packs on the chain, trading cards just hit peak convenience,” to which it replied, “You get it.”

“STFU, Coinbase is going to partner with and onboard everything on earth,” another wrote, to which Coinbase responded, “Well, we are the Everything Exchange.”

Based on this post, it looks like Coinbase users will soon be able to open digital card packs, with the option to place those cards in a digital ‘vault’ or receive their physical equivalent by mail.

However, another reply from Coinbase suggests there’ll be some additional features at play; one user wrote, “The vaulting aspect is the real game changer here,” to which it replied, “And there’s more…”

For now, details remain sparse. We don’t know how Coinbase’s status as a crypto platform will impact its attempt at a pack-opening service, nor how it intends to grade said cards or provide proof of ownership. Will these pulls come from pre-opened packs? Who’s to say.

It’s also worth noting that such a service, sans cryptocurrency, already exists; as pointed out by Dexerto , Gamestop’s Power Packs program also features a digital option, allowing customers to open mystery packs online and receive those cards’ physical counterparts.

Gamestop assures its buyers that every digital pack contains a "real, authenticated item” that they can either hold in their digital PSA vault, have shipped to them, or take advantage of its instant buyback program and use those funds to purchase another card pack. It remains to be seen if Coinbase will provide similar guarantees.

Coinbase’s proposed pack-opening platform comes on the heels of Pokémon’s 30th Anniversary celebration, which has shone a spotlight on the ever-growing hype around the card collecting scene, as well as the scalpers who have caused chaos during its special merchandise and card launches.

For instance, the special 30th Anniversary card pack drops at retailers like Target and other shops prompted long lines outside stores as mobs of fans showed up for the chance at snagging some packs for themselves, with some even ‘reserving’ spots in line by setting out chairs with no one sitting in them.

articles.title: Obsession Director Curry Barker's Next Film, Anything But Ghosts, Gets May 2027 Theatrical Release
articles.summary: Obsession director Curry Barker’s next film, Anything But Ghosts, is coming to theaters next year.
articles.body:
Obsession director Curry Barker’s next film, Anything But Ghosts, is coming to theaters next year.

Anything But Ghosts comes to the silver screen on May 7, 2027. The film takes place in the same universe as Obsession , but is classified as a horror-comedy that follows a different cast of characters entirely — though they also go through some seriously spooky stuff.

Barker’s next flick stars Bryce Dallas Howard, Aaron Paul, Violet McGraw, Chris Reinache, and Cooper Tomlinson, who notably played Bear’s best friend, Ian, in Obsession, as well as Barker himself. Anything But Ghosts centers around two fake paranormal investigators who are finally confronted with some actual, real-life ghosts (or would that be ‘real-afterlife’ ghosts?), causing things to “spiral wildly and terrifyingly out of control,” as per an official press release.

Speaking on a June episode of Raiders of the Lost Podcast , Tomlinson confirmed that he and Curry are playing the two phony ghost hunters, and described the film as “if Key and Peele walked into Hereditary.”

“It’s a buddy comedy, you know, about these two guys, and it turns really scary,” he said. “You know, it’s about these con artist ghost hunters who encounter real ghosts, and then they have to step up and be the thing that they promised this family.”

Both Barker and Tomlinson are producing and co-writing the film, which is produced by Focus Features and Blumhouse-Atomic Monster. Focus holds the movie’s worldwide rights, and Universal Pictures International is handling international distribution for the studio. This is the second time Focus and Blumhouse-Atomic Monster have worked together on a Curry Barker film; the two production houses also collaborated on Obsession, which released to rave reviews earlier this year.

Barker’s next offering has a lot to live up to; Obsession became one of the world's most profitable films compared to its budget in history, receiving critical acclaim and becoming an instant horror classic. Inde Navarrette’s standout performance as Nikki catapulted her to international fame, helping her land the role of Rogue in Marvel’s X-Men reboot , and put Barker in the hotseat for studios looking to get in on his future projects.

If you’ve ever watched Barker and Tomlinson’s humorous YouTube videos , you can safely assume that their delightful chemistry will get ample time to shine in Anything But Ghosts. With hard-hitters like Breaking Bad’s Aaron Paul and Jurassic World’s Bryce Dallas Howard in the mix, there’s no telling what hijinks these two will get up to, but we can almost guarantee it’ll be hilarious. And given how creepy Obsession managed to be on such a small budget, it feels like the Hereditary -ness of it all might also give us a few good scares, too.

articles.title: Jennifer Lawrence to Star in Zach Cregger’s Sci-Fi Thriller The Flood
articles.summary: Zach Cregger’s next movie, a science fiction thriller called The Flood, is set to release in theaters on August 11, 2028.
articles.body:
Zach Cregger’s next movie, a science fiction thriller called The Flood , is set to release in theaters on August 11, 2028.

Cregger is writing, producing, and directing the film, which will star Jennifer Lawrence, as confirmed by Variety on September 29, 2026.

Warner Bros. and New Line Cinema are slated to distribute the movie, which is being produced by Amblin Entertainment and Vertigo Entertainment's Roy Lee and Miri Yoon.

Thus far, other cast members and specific plot details have been kept secret, but Cregger has given us a few insights into what we can expect from his forthcoming sci-fi flick. Speaking to Men’s Health in mid-September, Cregger revealed that the movie is 'similar' to Stanley Kubrick’s 2001: A Space Odyssey .

“I'm not comparing [The Flood] to 2001, because I think 2001 is a true masterpiece in every sense of the word. But there's a bizarreness to that movie that's really undeniable, and it's also a horror movie. I think 2001 is a really thrilling horror movie about human nature, and obviously about artificial intelligence, but it asks big questions. And I think, in that way, there's some similarity with Flood,” he said.

Based on these remarks, we can safely assume that The Flood has something to do with AI, human nature, and big-picture concepts — but one thing he confirmed was that The Flood is very specifically not a horror movie.

“It unfolds in a very unique way that I'm really proud of. It's disturbing, but it's not a horror movie, although there are horror scenes in it. It feels intimidating to me. I'm still not really sure how to make it, but I think that's a good thing,” he clarified.

“It's hard to talk about it without talking about the story. I’m thrilled to have the opportunity to make that movie. I’m in love with that story in a really unique way."

This news comes hot on the heels of Cregger’s Resident Evil adaptation, which released to overwhelmingly positive reviews among both fans of the games and film critics alike. It became the single most-successful Resident Evil movie ever, and even helped boost sales for Resident Evil 2 Remake by 50% on PlayStation 5.

Cregger is best known for horror flicks like Barbarian and Weapons , so it’ll be interesting to see his take on a science fiction thriller. He isn’t the only big director in the horror space with exciting news to share, either, as Obsession director Curry Barker’s next movie, a horror-comedy titled Anything But Ghosts, has received a theatrical release date for May 7, 2027.

articles.title: Everything Coming to Amazon Prime Video in October
articles.body:
Amazon Prime subscribers will be getting a lot out of the Prime Video streaming service this October. This is largely thanks to some of the biggest movie franchises like James Bond, Rocky, and Indiana Jones making their way to the platform starting on October 1. Oh and there's also a new miniseries based on Stepen King's Carrie that could be really good.

If you're wondering how to make the most of your Prime Video subscription next month, I've curated a quick selection of movies and shows that are absolutely worth your time. You can also jump to the full list of October releases to see the full breakdown by day.

If you've been following James Bond news over the past couple of years, it shouldn't be a surprise to see the spy films coming to Prime Video this month. Amazon paid $20 million for the Bond franchise back in 2025 and is now working on a new movie. The first step? Finding the next James Bond actor .

As of October 1 you'll be able to stream the entire James Bond movie collection from every Bond actor to ever play the role.

The John Wick franchise has some of the best action movie scenes of all time. Keanu Reeves delivers a terrific performance as the grizzled assassin just trying to retire, and the series has only gotten better with time. John Wick: Chapter 4 was one of those rare movies we gave a perfect 10 out of 10 , proving sequels can be terrific if done right. All four John Wick movies will be coming to Prime Video starting on October 1.

Four of the five Indiana Jones movies will be coming to Prime Video. The only film being skipped over will be the latest one, Dial of Destiny, which is arguably the worst in the series. IGN gave the fifth and final film a 4 out of 10 in our review , saying: "Earnest final efforts from Harrison Ford and John Williams couldn’t rescue a movie so directionless and haphazard."

With most of the films finally coming to a streaming service outside of Disney+ and Paramount+, October is the perfect time to have yourself an Indy movie marathon .

Stephen King's Carrie has already been adapted several times since, but Amazon is bringing it back once again. Prime Video's Carrie will be an eight episode miniseries starring Sissy Spacek. The new series is led by Mike Flanagan, who has continued to make a name for himself with popular horror projects like The Haunting of Hill House and Doctor Sleep . All eight episodes of the series will be dropping on Prime Video on October 7.

The Scream franchise has been experiencing a true renaissance, starting with Scream 5 back in 2022. This year we saw the release of the seventh movie in the series, and it's finally coming to a streaming service. Our 6 out of 10 review of Scream 7 wasn't as positive as our review of the last movie, but we did find it overall worth watching if you're a fan of the franchise.

articles.title: GTA 6's Game of the Year Chances Have Been Called Into Question
articles.summary: GTA 6 may not even be eligible for Game of the Year at The Game Awards this year.
articles.body:
GTA 6 may not even be eligible for Game of the Year at The Game Awards this year.

Actress, games writer, and former games journalist Alanah Pearce stated during a recent live stream that she doesn't think GTA 6 has a good chance of sweeping at The Game Awards this year due to the timing of its release. Pearce stated that the cutoff date for games being eligible for TGA nominations has historically taken place around the same time as GTA 6's release date this year. And while some have countered her insights by noting that the cutoff last year was November 21, two days after GTA 6 will release this year, there are still some valid questions raised.

Most notably: Would anyone even be able to feasibly finish GTA 6 before voting on nominees? And if not, would the jury be willing to vote on it without finishing it? That would certainly raise a lot of ethical concerns over the voting process. However, there are some ways that Rockstar's chances could be increased. For starters, Geoff Keighley, the overseer of The Game Awards, could simply push the voting deadlines back. It's certainly not impossible, as Keighley does love a good show, and GTA 6 sweeping would lead to a lot of eyes on the event.

Another possibility is that Rockstar Games could give jury members a significant headstart to play the game prior to the cutoff date. As of right now, it's hard to say what Rockstar's plans are for reviewers, but such a strategy would certainly give it an easier time securing a nomination. It's a lot of ifs, though.

We can only speculate, but if for whatever reason GTA 6 isn't eligible this year, it could try again in 2027... and it might still have a chance. Rockstar Games is heavily rumored to launch GTA 6's online mode next year , which will undoubtedly give the game a massive second wind. If that's enough to contend with other heavy hitters, such as Naughty Dog's Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet , Rockstar could be in the 2027 awards race.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: Original God of War Creator Defends Laufey's Creative Director From Harassment After His Critical Remarks Go Viral
articles.summary: David Jaffe, the creator, co-writer, and director for the original God of War game, has cleared up his viral comments about Ariel Lawrence, creative director for Laufey.
articles.body:
David Jaffe, the creator, co-writer, and director for the original God of War game, has cleared up his viral comments about Ariel Lawrence, creative director for Laufey.

Ariel Lawrence has been with the God of War franchise since its very first game — but creator David Jaffe, who left the series behind in 2007 to form his own studio, says he never got along with her during his time at Santa Monica Studio.

He described their contentious work relationship in a September 2026 live stream while reacting to footage for God of War Laufey , where he claimed their personalities clashed and that he didn’t feel as though she was truly passionate about the games they were making.

“I have no problem with female directors at all,” he began. “This woman started as an assistant producer back when we were making the first God of War. Her and I never got along. She thought I was kind of obnoxious and I thought she was pretentious. She didn’t put the audience first.

“People that I didn’t get along with on God of War were people, in my opinion, who were more about, ‘I wanna do well in the corporate world… I want to play the game,’ versus, ‘I’m here with a vision and I will f**kin’ fight you for that vision.’ There was a lack of passion I felt from her, and she was also kind of a judgy asshole, to me.”

Jaffe also slammed Cory Barlog for making Laufey in the first place — which he called a “stupid” game — and asked why he couldn’t “sit Ariel down and say, ‘This isn’t ready.’”

Jaffe’s comments unsurprisingly went viral, sparking a debate within the God of War fanbase and the broader gaming community in general. Not long afterward, Jaffe took to Twitter/X to expound upon his remarks, where he called out those using his statement to harass Lawrence online.

“Look, I personally didn't like Ariel and I don't THINK she cared much for me back when we worked together. Oil and Water, just very different types of people. And honestly, she was probably more liked on the team than I was. You see, if you haven't noticed, I can be, as my ex-wife says, 'a lot,’” he wrote.

“And so in this video, I was responding/sharing that aspect of our time working together. That's the only way I would ever talk about former colleagues, be it good or bad experiences. For people to use my experience with Ariel as an excuse/launching pad to make personal attacks on her is just low and s**tty.

"She's a real person — just like you — with a life and feelings and people who care for her and who love her, and it just seems really f**king cruel to do that. Plus, have you looked in your own mirror? I've looked in mine; that s**t's scary! You see this f**king beard?!? Good lord, I'm days away from moving to the North Pole…”

Look, I personally didn't like Ariel and I don't THINK she cared much for me back when we worked together. Oil and Water, just very different types of people. And honestly, she was probably more liked on the team than I was. You see, if you haven't noticed, I can be, as my… — David Jaffe (@davidscottjaffe) September 29, 2026

Laufey has, unfortunately, been a target for the online rage machine, and Jaffe's remarks are adding more fuel to the fire. Trolls’ remarks about Deborah Ann Woll’s appearance and their outrage over the fact that a woman is leading a God of War game totally overwhelmed gaming circles on social media when it was first revealed in June, and this finger-pointing doesn’t appear to have stopped, but rather simply slowed down.

Other games have since taken the brunt of the internet’s apparent boredom, as evidenced by the debate surrounding Insomniac’s Wolverine . But still, Laufey has managed to catch strays in this regard, with The Last of Us director Bruce Straley using it as an example of why modern AAA games no longer “excite” him (though he later apologized for this comment ).

God of War Laufey releases on February 16, 2027, exclusively for PlayStation 5.

articles.title: 'The Train Isn't Stopping' — Diablo 4 Director Promises the Game Will Still Receive Support Well After Diablo 5 Launches
articles.summary: Diablo 4 director Brent Gibson is telling fans not to worry about the game after Diablo 5’s announcement sparked concerns about the former title’s lifespan.
articles.body:
Diablo 4 director Brent Gibson is telling fans not to worry about the game after Diablo 5’s announcement sparked concerns about the former title’s lifespan.

Diablo 5’s reveal at Blizzcon 2026 left fans equal parts excited and worried. Of course, players were pumped for a new Diablo game — but with Diablo 4 having just launched in 2023, the reveal of a new game so soon felt like a death knell for the one they were still playing.

But Brent Gibson, director of Diablo 4, says there’s nothing to fuss about. Speaking with Icy Veins , Gibson outlined some plans for the game’s future content, saying it will continue to receive support well after 5’s release.

Diablo: Dawn of Hatred #1 Preview Gallery

“I have an analogy,” he began. “If you’re wearing a sign in the middle of Times Square saying, ‘The end is nigh,’ the end is not nigh. We have a lot coming. We have [the] Amazon [class] coming down the road. The train isn’t stopping.

“One of the things I love about our world is we are not a series of games. We are a universe. We are even adding to Diablo 2 with the Warlock. It’s one of the few franchises where we have the luxury of continued play, and we know our communities.

“If you’re worried, don’t sweat it, because we’re going to be making content for a long time. But we are excited about Diablo 5. We’ve got a show coming. Gone are the years of waiting a decade for more content. It’s a great place to be.”

More specifically, Gibson said Blizzard is planning on supporting seasons for Diablo 4 “as long as the community continues to show up” for it, specifically mentioning the ongoing support for Diablo 2 and Diablo 3.

“There are still people who play those games, and as long as you’re showing up, we’re going to continue to be making content," he assured.

As Gibson mentioned, Diablo 4 is getting the Amazon class in the first half of 2027. With three more years to go until Diablo 5 is released, there’s still plenty of time for developers to flesh out the title with even more classes and experiences — something they spoke about during a dedicated Diablo panel at Blizzcon this year.

“Diablo 4 has bright support,” Diablo 5 director Joe Shely said . “It's fully supported by the team. We were just announcing earlier today, coming to Diablo 4, the Amazon, the Season of Hell's legacy, Diablo 4 is coming to Switch 2, and there will continue to be ongoing support for Diablo 4. There's many reasons for players to keep playing.”

“We have dedicated teams for each of those games because those games are important to us and they're really important for our community,” production director Tiffany Wat added. “I think it really gives us a really great opportunity to be able to collaborate together, to talk with one another. Even though we might be distinct teams, we still work together quite closely because ultimately we are making games for the Diablo community. I think it's the best time to be a Diablo fan.”

For more Diablo news, you can check out our interview with the developers here, as well as catch up with their reaction to the series' animated show coming to Netflix .

articles.title: Digger Ad Trolls Bad Reviews for New Tom Cruise Film: ‘F*** Those People!’
articles.summary: Warner Bros. has posted a social media ad highlighting the deeply divided critical response to Tom Cruise and director Alejandro G. Iñárritu’s new film Digger just hours after the review embargo was lifted.
articles.body:
Well, that was fast. Warner Bros. has posted a social media ad highlighting the deeply divided critical response to Tom Cruise and director Alejandro G. Iñárritu’s new film Digger just hours after the review embargo was lifted.

The movie, which opens in theaters October 2, currently has a “rotten” score of 52% on review aggregator Rotten Tomatoes and a score of 44 on Metacritic . (Cruise’s lowest-rated film on Rotten Tomatoes is Cocktail with 11%.)

“The ad begins with a quote from X user @thejonathansim: ‘Digger is an ambitious film sure to polarize audiences.’ It then cuts to a clip from the film featuring Cruise’s Digger Rockwell saying, ‘You know what? F--- those people!’ The rest of the ad shows positive and negative phrases from various reactions to the film flipping back and forth on screen including ‘unpleasant’ and ‘masterpiece,’ ‘baffling’ and ‘brilliant,’ and ‘insufferable’ and ‘magnificent’.”

IGN’s Michael Calabro was on the mixed side in his Digger review , awarding the film an “okay” score of 6 out of 10:

“Digger's satire may not change your thinking on global warming, but there are excellent performances and more than a few laughs… Digger is far from a must-watch, and if the trailer has you feeling skeptical, save your money. The theater experience won't change your mind, and the laughs that are there still will be when it hits HBO Max.”

Billed as “a comedy of catastrophic proportions,” the satire stars a nearly unrecognizable Tom Cruise as tycoon Digger Rockwell, whose oil drilling operations spark a global disaster.
